 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the Insurance Company as against respondents on the ground that the claim petition was dismissed against respondent No.2 before the Tribunal, hence, it is held there is no question on the part of the insurance company to indemnify the owner.

2. The claim petition was filed by the claimant seeking compensation having sustained injuries in the road accident that occurred on 24.01.2016 at about 07.00 p.m. when he was riding Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 64-H-4430 near RES College, Neelagiri Thopu, Hegganahalli Main Road,
Bengaluru city, hit by another Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HT-1676.

The Tribunal NC:
2024:KHC:20660 has awarded compensation by fixing liability on the appellant/insurance company to pay the compensation.

3. The learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company submitted that before the Tribunal, the claim petition against respondent No.2/owner was dismissed on 17.08.2016 for not taking steps to serve of notice on respondent No.2/owner.

When the claim petition is dismissed against the owner,
then there is no question of indemnifying the owner by the insurance company.
Therefore, prays to allow the appeal.

4. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused the records.
5.

The points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
1. Whether, under the facts and circumstances involved in the case, when in the claim petition before the tribunal is dismissed against the owner of the offending vehicle M/S National Insurance Company Ltd vs Sri. sentences.text: then insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner?
2. What order?

While considering the records and order sheet maintained in the case before the tribunal, the claim petition was dismissed on 17.08.2016 against the owner of offending vehicle on the ground that claimant has not taken steps to serve notice to owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, claim petition was dismissed against respondent No.2/owner of the offending vehicle.
7. Insurance policy is contractual policy between the insurer and insured.
Primary liability is on the owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation when the tort is committed.
Insurance company comes into picture only when there is a contract of insurance between the insurer and insured.
Therefore, the liability of the insurance company is based on the contract of insurance by the insurance policy.
Therefore, the obligation is on the part of the insurance company is to indemnify the owner of vehicle.
But where the claim petition is dismissed against the owner then there is no question of indemnifying the owner.

Where there is valid existence of insurance policy, NC:
2024:KHC:20660 the liability is jointly and severally on the insurer and insured.
If any reasons, the claim petition is dismissed against the owner, then there would not be a question of indemnifying the owner by the insurance company.

Therefore, in this regard, upon the principle of above stated,
considering the present case, the claim petition against respondent No.2/owner of the offending vehicle was dismissed.
Therefore, when there would not be indemnification of insurance company to the owner of the vehicle then the insurance company is also not liable to pay compensation.
This principle of the law is lost sight by the Tribunal.
Hence, in case of dismissal of the claim petition against the owner of the offending vehicle then the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner.
Accordingly, I answer above mentioned points in the affirmative.
8. Hence, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.

The matter is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration by reserving liberty to claimant take steps against respondent No.2/owner and after getting service of notice to respondent No.2/owner the Tribunal shall consider the case afresh on merits as per law.

10. It is due to part committed by the claimant for not taking steps against respondent No.2/owner,
therefore, when the case would be reconsidering on the merits after remanding the case, then the insurance company is not liable to pay interest from date of the petition till today.
11.
If Tribunal would gives finding that the claimant entitled for interest
then it would be from today till realization by the insurance company.

12. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: ORDER i.
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is allowed.

The impugned judgment and award dated 11.08.2017 in MVC.No.1511/2016 passed by the VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (SCCH-5) Bengaluru, is set aside and remanded to the Tribunal for afresh consideration in accordance with law.
iii. Both parties are at liberty to adduce further evidence, if they are in so desire.
All contentions are left open.
iv. The claimant is not entitled to interest from the date of the filing of the petition before the Tribunal till today.
v. The claimant and insurance company shall appear before the Tribunal on 15.07.2024 without waiting for notice.
Issue notice to the owner of vehicle.
vi. The Tribunal is directed to dispose of the petition within 9 months from 15.07.2024.
vii. The amount deposited by the appellant shall be refunded to the appellant in accordance with law.
NC: 2024:KHC:20660 viii.
Registry is directed to transmit the TCR along with copy of this order to the Tribunal forthwith.
